articles.title: The Temporal Flow of Interaction: Interpersonal Synchronization and Alliance Perception Across Session Parts
articles.abstract: During psychotherapy, patient and therapist tend to spontaneously synchronize their vocal pitch, bodily movements, and even their physiological processes. In the present article, we consider how this pervasive phenomenon may shed new light on the therapeutic relationship- or alliance- and its role within psychotherapy. We first review clinical research on the alliance and the multidisciplinary area of interpersonal synchrony. We then integrate both literatures in the Interpersonal Synchrony (In-Sync) model of psychotherapy. According to the model, the alliance is grounded in the coupling of patient and therapist's brains. Because brains do not interact directly, movement synchrony may help to establish inter-brain coupling. Inter-brain coupling may provide patient and therapist with access to another's internal states, which facilitates common understanding and emotional sharing. Over time, these interpersonal exchanges may improve patients' emotion-regulatory capacities and related therapeutic outcomes. We discuss the empirical assessment of interpersonal synchrony and review preliminary research on synchrony in psychotherapy. Finally, we summarize our main conclusions and consider the broader implications of viewing psychotherapy as the product of two interacting brains.
articles.keywords: Psychology; Alliance; Interpersonal communication; Association; Perception; Task; Session; Bayesian probability; Variance
articles.summary: 本研究提出了一个心理治疗中的人际同步模型，探讨患者与治疗师在声音、动作等非言语行为上的自发同步如何促进治疗联盟。模型认为这种同步有助于建立大脑耦合，增强情绪分享和理解，从而提升患者的情绪调节能力与治疗效果。

articles.title: Multimodal social synchrony: Neural, physiological, attentional, and aesthetic alignment as predictors of friendship.
articles.journal: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts
articles.publish_info: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts, 2026-07-06
articles.abstract: This study demonstrates that social bonds are grounded not only in cultural or cognitive commonalities but also in multilayered neurophysiological and behavioral synchronization processes. Pairs of friends and strangers were evaluated while viewing aesthetic and spatial stimuli using electroencephalography, galvanic skin response, eye tracking, and facial expression analysis. Five primary synchronization metrics—neural (electroencephalography phase-locking value), autonomic (galvanic skin response correlation), perceptual-attentional (area of interest overlap and scanpath similarity), and expressive (facial synchrony)—were integrated into a logistic regression-based multimodal classification model. The model accurately predicted whether individuals were friends or strangers and achieved a significant performance gain over single-modality measures. Findings address the question "Does shared preference foster friendship, or does friendship shape preferences?" by proposing a bidirectional mechanism: Shared preferences initiate social attraction, whereas friendship progressively aligns aesthetic and spatial perception patterns. This proof-of-concept framework may inform future interdisciplinary research on social synchrony across social neuroscience and environmental psychology; however, broader applied use will require replication in independent and more naturalistic settings.
articles.keywords: Psychology; Cognitive psychology; Social psychology; Creativity; Social relation; Communication; Perception; Multimodality
articles.summary: 本研究通过整合神经、生理、注意力和面部表情分析的多模态同步指标，发现这些指标能有效预测社交关系中的友谊。研究提出共同偏好引发社交吸引，而友谊则对齐审美和感知模式，揭示了双向影响机制。

articles.title: Unconscious mental content in implicit evaluation: Evidence from misprediction.
articles.authors: Benedek Kurdi, David E Melnikoff, Adam Morris
articles.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
articles.publish_info: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2026-07-09
articles.abstract: The tide is turning against a major idea in social psychology: that implicit evaluations reflect mental content that lies beyond conscious awareness. This view is being reconsidered in light of mounting evidence that people can predict their own implicit evaluations with high accuracy. However, there are reasons to question whether such predictive accuracy reflects introspective access. First, prior studies have relied almost exclusively on familiar targets (e.g., racial groups), allowing predictions to be informed by background knowledge (e.g., knowing that a group is stigmatized) rather than introspection. Second, implicit and explicit evaluations have been highly correlated in prior work, enabling accurate predictions simply by assuming that implicit evaluations mirror explicit ones. Here, we report eight experiments (five pre-registered; N = 6,794) designed to minimize these nonintrospective routes to predictive accuracy. We introduced participants to novel targets and shifted implicit and explicit evaluations of these targets in opposite directions, rendering explicit evaluations an unreliable cue. Under these conditions, predictive accuracy ranged from low to nonexistent; participants frequently anticipated shifts in their implicit evaluations in the opposite direction of the actual change. These results generalized across two learning paradigms (impression formation and attribute conditioning), two implicit evaluation measures (Implicit Association Test and evaluative priming task), and between-participant and within-participant designs. We consider multiple interpretations of these findings, including the possibility that implicit evaluations reflect mental content that is largely or even entirely inaccessible to conscious awareness.
articles.keywords: Psychology; Implicit-association test; Priming; Unconscious mind; Social psychology; Implicit attitude; Cognitive psychology; Implicit personality theory; Mental representation; Association; Test
articles.summary: 本研究通过八个实验探讨隐性评价是否反映无意识心理内容。实验引入新目标并将隐性与显性评价向相反方向操纵，发现参与者对隐性评价变化的预测准确性很低，经常错误预期变化方向。结果表明隐性评价可能主要基于无意识的心理内容。

articles.title: Beyond synchrony: Why disengagement can sometimes be the healthiest choice.
articles.abstract: Synchrony can support psychotherapy by enhancing rapport, emotional attunement, trust, and attachment. However, synchrony is not inherently beneficial: In some contexts, excessive or maladaptive synchrony may reinforce conformity, dependence, or dysfunctional relational patterns. We argue that the clinical meaning of synchrony depends on the interaction between interpersonal context, the individual's trait-like synchrony signature, and state-like deviations from that baseline. From this perspective, both synchrony and disengagement-including asynchronous interaction-may be therapeutically meaningful when they promote autonomy, differentiation, and adaptive change.
articles.keywords: Disengagement theory; Psychology; Cognitive psychology; Social psychology; Cognitive science; Perception; Developmental psychology; Creativity; Cognition
articles.summary: 本研究探讨了心理治疗中同步性的双重作用，指出同步性并非总是有益，有时可能强化适应不良模式。论文认为同步性的临床意义取决于人际背景、个体特征和状态偏差，同步性和脱离在促进自主性、分化和适应性改变时可能具有治疗意义。

articles.title: People in more individualist cultures are more motivated to make others feel better.
articles.authors: Shir Ginosar Yaari, Yulia Chentsova-Dutton, Michaela Riediger, Antje Rauers, Min Young Kim, Yuri Miyamoto, Allon Vishkin, Julia Anne Freitag, Jan Cieciuch, Mariana Gurevich, Maria Padun, Nevin Solak, Xiaoqin Wang, Jiang Qiu, Aldo Alvarez-Risco, Alessandro Alberto Rossi, Yaniv Hanoch, Yukiko Uchida, Claudio Vaz Torres, Thiago Gomes Nascimento, Asghar Afshar Jahanshahi, Rakesh Singh, Babita Singh, Shanmukh V Kamble, Sieun An, Vivian Dzokoto, Adote Anum, Stefania Mannarini, María Isabel Huerta-Carvajal, Erika Galindo-Bello, Verónica Janneth García Ibarra, Arobindu Dash, Maya Tamir
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.publish_info: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, Vol. 123, Issue 27, 2026-07-07
articles.abstract: In many Western cultures, trying to make others feel better is considered critical for psychological health and social relationships. However, given that people think about emotions and relationships differently across cultures, the desirability, means, and benefits of making others feel better may also vary by culture. In two multicountry survey studies (Study 1: N = 3,154, 13 countries; Study 2: N = 3,503, 17 countries) and in a daily dairy study (Study 3: N = 243, 2 countries), we assessed motivation and strategies used for influencing others' and one's own emotions. To test whether potential cross-cultural differences in motivation and strategies in emotion regulation are unique to social interactions, we compared cultural differences in making others feel better to making oneself feel better. Across studies, cultural differences in influencing others' emotions were greater than those in influencing one's own emotions. Members of more individualist (vs. collectivist) cultures were more motivated to make others (but not themselves) feel better, were more likely to express care and less likely to encourage others to suppress their emotions or to ruminate. These patterns, in turn, were linked to an index of relationship closeness in an individualist (but not a collectivist) culture. These findings suggest that helping others feel better may not be equally desirable across cultures.
articles.keywords: culture; emotion regulation; interpersonal emotion regulation; motivation; relationships
articles.summary: 本研究通过两项多国调查和一项日记研究，考察了不同文化中人们影响他人情绪的动机与策略差异。发现个人主义文化中的人比集体主义文化中的人更有动力让他人感觉更好，并更倾向于表达关心而非鼓励抑制情绪；这些模式与关系亲密度的关联仅在个人主义文化中显著。

articles.title: Does gratitude moderate the bystander effect? A registered report.
articles.authors: Ryuji Oguni, Yukari Jessica Tham, Chikara Ishii
articles.abstract: The prosocial function of gratitude is well-established in bilateral situations. However, its role in situations with multiple potential benefactors is unclear. As the number of potential benefactors increases, prosocial decisions become more complex due to the diffusion of responsibility and uncertainty about others' intentions. In this registered report, we examined whether gratitude promotes prosocial behaviour in situations with multiple potential benefactors and whether it moderates the inhibitory effect of their increasing number. Participants (N = 867) were randomly assigned to gratitude, calm, or neutral conditions. They decided whether to allocate resources to a beneficiary in the presence of one, three, or five potential benefactors. The results demonstrated the bystander effect, showing that prosocial behaviour declined as the number of potential benefactors increased. Although gratitude promoted prosocial behaviour, it did not moderate the inhibitory effect of increasing the number of potential benefactors on prosocial behaviour. These findings reveal the effects and scope of gratitude's prosocial function, indicating that gratitude promotes prosocial behaviour but does not moderate the bystander effect.
articles.summary: 本研究通过注册报告考察了感恩情绪在有多位潜在受益者的情境中对亲社会行为的影响。结果表明，感恩促进了亲社会决策，但并未调节因潜在受益者数量增加而引起的旁观者效应，揭示了感恩亲社会功能的作用范围。

articles.title: Changes in facial expression recognition and well-being over time.
articles.authors: Marie Huc, Katie Bush, Lindsay Berrigan, Sylvia Cox, Natalia Jaworska
articles.abstract: Facial occlusion effects on emotion recognition are well-documented; however, improvements in recognition over time and relations with mental health changes remain unclear. This longitudinal study examined changes in recognition of occluded emotional faces and mental health features in a Canadian cohort (N = 128). After 3-4 months, participants showed greater accuracy in recognising most expressions and faster reaction time (RT) for fearful but slower RT for surprised faces. More daily "masked interactions" were related to slower RT for happy and sad faces but higher accuracy, suggesting a speed-accuracy trade-off. Increased depression symptoms were associated with greater accuracy for masked happy faces, while increased anxiety was associated with greater accuracy for happy and neutral faces. This study emphasises complex relations between masked emotion recognition and mental well-being, which can inform strategies for coping with social interaction restrictions.
articles.category: Emotion, Facial Expression, Emotion Perception, Face
articles.summary: 本研究通过纵向方法考察了面部遮挡下情绪识别随时间的变化及其与心理健康特征的关系，发现参与者识别被遮挡表情的准确性提高，反应时间因表情类型而异。每日戴口罩互动与情绪识别反应时间相关，而抑郁和焦虑症状的增加与对特定面孔识别准确性的提高相关，揭示了情绪识别与心理健康之间的复杂关联。

articles.title: He was called ugly, not me: valence and referent of social opinions do not impact face recognition but affect attribution of the opinion's target.
articles.authors: Amie J Durston, Myra A Fernandes, Roxane J Itier
articles.abstract: Remembering faces and their associated contexts is important for healthy social cognition. We used a social opinion paradigm to assess whether the valence and relevance (about the self or other) of expressed opinions influenced memory for faces and who the opinion was about. Participants (N = 144) read opinions varying in reference and valence (e.g. "She thinks your/his smile is beautiful/crooked") followed by neutral faces said to hold the opinion. Participants rated their feelings of valence and arousal, followed by a surprise old/new face recognition test. Face recognition was not influenced by the type of opinion. We also assessed accuracy of "reference attribution" for the social opinion. Participants reported whether the opinion was in reference to themselves or someone else. Reference attributions were more accurate for opinions directed toward others than oneself. Moreover, higher endorsement of symptoms of depression was linked to enhanced reference attribution accuracy for self-related contexts, while higher endorsement of anxiety symptoms was associated with lower attribution accuracy. Results suggest the influence of social context on memory depends on context valence and personal relevance, as well as participants' trait symptoms.
articles.keywords: Face Recognition; reference attribution; self-reference; social anxiety; social context
articles.summary: 本研究采用社会意见范式，考察了意见的情绪效价和参考性（针对自己或他人）对面孔识别和参考归因准确性的影响。结果发现，面孔识别不受意见类型影响，但参考归因准确性在意见指向他人时更高；此外，抑郁症状与自我相关上下文的归因准确性增强相关，而焦虑症状则与准确性降低相关。

articles.title: Bidirectional Cross-modal Fear Generalization: Semantic Similarity in Representation Space as a Foundational Mechanism.
articles.authors: Haoran Dou, Shanhe Du, Jonas Zaman, Kenny Yu, Ying Mei, Yiwen Qiu, Yi Lei
articles.abstract: Fear generalization is vital for human survival in the complex, multimodal environments. Despite extensive research on fear generalization within sensory modalities, our theoretical understanding of cross-modal generalization mechanisms remains unclear. To fill this gap, this study conducted two experiments (total N = 95) to investigate bidirectional cross-modality fear generalization in individuals with high and low anxiety levels: Experiment 1 used an auditory conditioned stimulus (CS) and visual generalized stimuli (GS), while Experiment 2 used a visual CS and auditory GS. Participants underwent fear conditioning and generalization tasks, measuring shock expectancy ratings, skin conductance responses, and prefrontal cortex activation via functional near-infrared spectroscopy. Critically, we demonstrate that fear generalized cross-modally in both directions-from auditory to visual and from visual to auditory-with auditory-to-visual generalization being significantly stronger than the reverse, indicating an asymmetric pattern. Furthermore, high-anxiety individuals exhibited elevated shock expectancy and skin conductance during generalization, alongside reduced medial prefrontal cortex activation. These findings demonstrate that semantic similarity in mental representational space fundamentally governs associative learning across sensory boundaries, and that bidirectional cross-modal fear generalization is asymmetrical. Moreover, we provide evidence of excessive cross-modality fear generalization in subclinical anxiety, enhancing understanding of anxiety mechanisms and fear-related disorders.
articles.keywords: Anxiety; Cross-modal; Fear generalization; Medial prefrontal cortex; Semantic similarity
articles.category: Emotion, Vocal Expression, Emotion Perception, Emotion Experience
articles.summary: 本研究通过两个实验探讨了双向跨模态恐惧泛化的机制，发现恐惧可以从听觉条件刺激泛化到视觉刺激，也可以从视觉条件刺激泛化到听觉刺激，但听觉到视觉的泛化更强，呈现不对称模式。高焦虑个体在恐惧泛化过程中表现出更高的预期和皮肤电反应，同时伴随内侧前额叶皮层激活降低，表明语义相似性是跨模态情绪学习的基础机制。

articles.title: Diminished Neural Responses for Greater Numbers of Lives at Risk and Lives Lost in Foreign Countries.
articles.abstract: Humanitarian crises fail to elicit responses proportional to their scale. Two psychological factors that may contribute to this problem are scope insensitivity, where concern fails to increase proportionally with the number of lives at risk, and home country bias. We studied these factors with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and behavioural measurement. Twenty-five participants completed scanning while viewing 'headlines': summaries describing a specified number (from one to tens of thousands) of lives that were at risk in either their home country or abroad, followed by information confirming their survival or death. Control trials presented analogous real financial risks. Whereas neural responses to financial risk scaled positively with risk magnitude, responses to life risk declined with larger numbers of lives at home and followed an 'inverted-U' in response to lives abroad: low for single lives abroad, higher for moderate numbers, but also low for the greatest numbers. Deaths only evoked stronger responses than survival for home country victims in regions previously associated with emotion derived from harm coming to other people. Independent willingness-to-pay ratings also demonstrated both biases. This study provides neural characterisations of scope insensitivity and home country bias when learning about lives at risk.
articles.keywords: Bias; Compassion; Death; Empathy; Risk; Scope Insensitivity
articles.summary: 本研究通过功能磁共振成像和行为测量，考察了范围不敏感性和本国偏见对人类在面对生命风险时神经反应的影响。结果表明，神经反应对生命风险的规模不敏感，且对本国受害者的反应更强，而国外受害者的反应呈非线性模式，行为评分也支持这些偏见。该研究为理解人道主义危机中的情绪反应提供了神经特征化证据。

articles.title: From "Always-On" to "Did I Miss It?": A Three-Country Study on Technological Work Experiences
articles.authors: Rachel Williamson Smith, Xinyu Hu, Yi-Ren Wang, Marcus J. Fila, Seulki Jang, Marcel Kern, Hyung In Park, Bo Yang
articles.abstract: The concept of fear of missing out (FoMO) has gained increasing popularity in the broader social psychology literature, yet scholarship on work-related FoMO is relatively nascent. We extend this literature to electronic availability expectations as a particularly relevant organizational antecedent of workplace FoMO. Although the existing literature suggests many downsides of FoMO, we posit that work-related FoMO may present a paradox resulting in both beneficial and harmful effects depending on the cognitive mechanisms at play and potential boundary conditions. In this cross-cultural study with a sample of K-12 teachers from South Korea, China, and Germany, we examined the implications of electronic availability expectations on teachers' work engagement through effects on workplace FoMO and rumination. Additionally, we explored how individual perceptions of a cultural dimension, uncertainty avoidance, may moderate these relationships. Latent change score analyses with three-wave longitudinal data collected from the three countries were performed. Electronic availability expectations predicted increases in workplace FoMO, which predicted increases in both types of rumination (affective rumination and problem-solving pondering). While affective rumination predicted decreases in engagement, problem-solving pondering predicted increases, suggesting a double-edged sword downstream effect. The indirect effect from electronic availability expectation to engagement was observed only via problem-solving pondering. Uncertainty avoidance moderated the effect of workplace FoMO on increases in problem-solving pondering; the effect was stronger for individuals with higher uncertainty avoidance. More similarities than differences were found across countries, suggesting the implications of electronic availability expectations on individuals' well-being might be a shared experience across cultures.
articles.keywords: Rumination; Psychology; Antecedent; Social psychology; Perception; Popularity; Sample; Scholarship; Work engagement; Industrial and organizational psychology
articles.summary: 本研究探讨了电子可用性期望如何通过工作相关错过恐惧（FoMO）影响教师的工作投入，并考察了个体不确定性回避的调节作用。通过对韩国、中国和德国K-12教师的三波纵向数据进行分析，发现电子可用性期望增加FoMO，进而提升情感反刍和问题解决沉思；情感反刍降低工作投入，问题解决沉思则提高投入，呈现双刃剑效应，且跨文化相似性多于差异。

articles.title: How Does Digital Connection Shape Cultural Adaptation? Differentiated Social Media Use, Intercultural Communication Self-Efficacy, and Adaptation Among International Students in China
articles.authors: Yang Xin, Deng Shusheng, Hu Weina, Deng Yan
articles.abstract: Evidence regarding the adaptive role of social media in acculturation remains fragmented, often overlooking behavioral nuances and contextual constraints. This study examined a moderated mediation model disentangling how three types of social media use—passive, active social, and active non-social—are associated with psychological and sociocultural adaptation through intercultural communication self-efficacy. Participants were 2,478 international students in China ( M = 23.67 years, SD = 3.82 years) who completed a multi-language survey. Structural equation modeling indicated that active social and active non-social use were positively associated with adaptation outcomes via enhanced intercultural communication self-efficacy, whereas passive use showed no significant association with efficacy beliefs. Furthermore, perceived cultural distance significantly moderated these indirect pathways; the adaptive associations between active engagement and self-efficacy were substantially attenuated for students perceiving high cultural disparity. These findings challenge universalist assumptions of digital empowerment, identifying intercultural communication self-efficacy as a core cognitive engine and perceived cultural distance as a critical boundary condition in digital acculturation.
articles.keywords: Acculturation; Intercultural communication; Adaptation; Social media; Social psychology; Psychology; Sociocultural evolution; Structural equation modeling; Mediation; Digital media
articles.summary: 本研究探讨了社交媒体使用类型（被动、主动社交、主动非社交）如何通过跨文化沟通自我效能影响在中国国际学生的心理和文化适应。结构方程模型分析发现，主动社交和主动非社交使用通过增强跨文化沟通自我效能正向预测适应结果，而被动使用无显著关联；感知文化距离显著调节这些间接路径，高文化距离感知会削弱适应效应。这些发现挑战了数字赋能的普遍性，指出跨文化沟通自我效能是核心认知机制，感知文化距离是关键边界条件。

articles.title: Perceived Pain Sensitivity and Treatment Recommendations for Socially Mobile Individuals: The Mediating Role of Perceived Tenacity
articles.authors: Zhijie Xie, Fangfang Wen, Lujun Shen, Chen Liu, Lei Yang
articles.abstract: While prior research shows that higher-class individuals are perceived as more sensitive to pain than lower-class individuals, little is known about how perceptions of pain are shaped by changes in social class. Across a pilot study and five experiments with Chinese and U.S. participants (N = 1,202), we investigated whether social mobility direction influences judgments of pain sensitivity and treatment, and whether perceived tenacity serves as a mediating mechanism. Results indicated that although Chinese and U.S. participants perceived higher-class individuals as more pain-sensitive, they judged upwardly mobile individuals as less sensitive to pain than downwardly mobile individuals. This effect was driven by the attribution of greater tenacity to upwardly mobile targets, which in turn predicted lower pain sensitivity ratings and fewer pain treatment recommendations. These findings reveal a novel psychological pathway through which dynamic social class information shapes pain perception and treatment decisions, extending the literature beyond static class-based stereotypes.
articles.keywords: pain perception; pain treatment; social class; social mobility; tenacity
articles.summary: 本研究通过中国和美国参与者的实验，探讨了社会流动性方向对疼痛敏感性感知和治疗建议的影响，并揭示了坚韧感的中介作用。结果发现，向上流动的个体被感知为疼痛敏感性较低，这归因于归因于更高的坚韧感，从而导致疼痛治疗推荐减少。该研究扩展了社会阶级刻板印象的文献，展示了动态社会信息如何通过心理路径塑造疼痛感知。

articles.title: Bystander Reactions to Economic Abuse: The Role of Moral Evaluation and Victim Blaming
articles.authors: Stefano Pagliaro, Theofilos Gkinopoulos, Attilio Di Crescenzo, Ilaria Giovannelli, Manuel Teresi, Federica Spaccatini, Maria Giuseppina Pacilli
articles.journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
articles.publish_info: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 2026-07-10
articles.abstract: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) is a worldwide public health issue. While most research has focused on victims' experiences and the consequences of physical and sexual IPV, less is known about how laypeople perceive and interpret episodes of IPV, particularly economic abuse, or how these perceptions shape their responses, such as moral evaluations, victim-blaming, helping behavior, and support for collective action. We address this gap by applying the bystander approach to examine the factors that influence social evaluation of economic abuse, including the role of contextual information about the victim, and specifically to investigate reactions, such as hiding financial information, to economic abuse. In Study 1 (correlational, N = 204) participants read a fictitious newspaper article in which a woman was verbally assaulted by her husband after he discovered she had secretly saved money in a separate bank account. We provided preliminary evidence that the less people represented economic abuse as a form of violence, the more likely they were to perceive the victim as immoral and blame her: Consequently, they were less inclined to help and support her and to engage in collective action to tackle the IPV more generally. In Study 2 (experimental, N = 274), participants who read that the victim saved money for self-oriented (vs. family-oriented) motivation evaluated her as less moral, blamed her, and were less inclined to help her and to engage in collective action. In Study 3 (experimental, N = 376), participants who read that the victim saved money as a reaction to previous economic abuse evaluated the victim as more moral, and as a consequence they blamed her to a less extent, and were more inclined to help and support her and to engage in collective action. We discuss potential implications for IPV policies and campaigns, which often overlook economic abuse and how moral biases shape public reactions.
articles.keywords: Blame; Social psychology; Psychology; Action; Collective action; Bystander effect; Perception; Suicide prevention; Newspaper; Poison control
articles.summary: 本研究通过三项实验考察了旁观者对亲密伴侣间经济虐待的反应。研究发现，人们对经济虐待的认知、受害者的储蓄动机（自我导向 vs. 家庭导向）以及虐待背景（是否作为先前虐待的反应）显著影响其道德评价、受害者责备、帮助意向和集体行动支持。这些结果揭示了道德偏见如何塑造公众反应，为相关干预政策提供了启示。

articles.title: Older Sibling Prosocial Behavior Toward Younger Siblings During Adolescence: A Multi-Informant Multi-Method Investigation
articles.authors: Christy R. Rogers, Eva H. Telzer
articles.journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
articles.publish_info: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 2026-07-10
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a time of increasing propensity to engage in prosocial behaviors toward family, with more recent work showing this proclivity toward siblings specifically. Sibling warmth and constructive problem-solving have been shown to promote adolescent well-being in several domains, but their contribution to adolescent prosocial decision-making towards siblings is unclear. Using multi-informant multi-methods data from 45 adolescent sibling pairs (older sibling: M age = 14.5; younger sibling: M age = 12.1) across time, this study examined whether dyadic sibling problem-solving (self-reported by both siblings) and observed warmth between siblings (coded from dyadic interactions) contributed to older "siblings" prosocial behavior toward young siblings (measured with an experimental task). We found a significant moderation, such that more constructive problem-solving predicted more prosocial decisions from older siblings to their younger siblings, but only when observed older sibling warmth toward younger siblings was high. These findings highlight the complex nature of relational processes in shaping older sibling prosociality toward younger siblings.
articles.keywords: Prosocial behavior; Sibling; Psychology; Developmental psychology; Sibling relationship; Volunteer work; Constructive; Helping behavior; Late childhood
articles.summary: 本研究考察了青少年期年长兄弟姐妹对年幼兄弟姐妹的亲社会行为，采用多信息多方法数据。发现二元兄弟姐妹问题解决和观察到的温暖对亲社会决策有贡献，具体表现为更多建设性问题解决预测更多亲社会决策，但仅在观察到的年长兄弟姐妹温暖较高时才显著。这突显了关系过程在塑造亲社会行为中的复杂性。

articles.title: AI-Generated Empathy: Opportunities, Limits, and Future Directions
articles.authors: Desmond C. Ong, Amit Goldenberg, Michael Inzlicht, Anat Perry
articles.abstract: Greater numbers of people are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) for empathy and emotional support. Here, we review and synthesize recent empirical work on how people perceive empathy from AI versus from humans. Growing evidence points to two dueling effects and a paradox: AI produces language that is rated higher in empathy than language written by humans, but when people perceive text as coming from AI versus a human, they rate it as less empathic. However, despite sometimes rating AI more empathic or having to wait for human empathy, people still show a preference for human empathy. This emerging literature carries significant implications for fundamental research on empathy and for public discourse as the use of AI for emotional support continues to grow.
articles.keywords: Empathy; Focus; Psychology; Social psychology; Empirical research; Emotional intelligence; Work; Empirical evidence
articles.summary: 本研究综述了人们如何感知AI与人类提供的同理心，发现AI生成的语言被评为比人类更具同理心，但当人们意识到文本来自AI时，其同理心评分反而降低。尽管如此，人们仍表现出对人类同理心的偏好。这一新兴文献对同理心的基础研究和AI在情感支持中的应用具有重要启示。

articles.title: The Benefits of Prosocial Behavior for Mental and Physical Health: A Neuroscience Approach
articles.authors: Naomi I. Eisenberger, Russell Noble, Maria Naclerio
articles.abstract: Prosocial behaviors, or actions intended to benefit others, embody the most selfless aspects of our nature. However, these behaviors can also benefit the giver. Prior work suggests that prosocial behavior can generate feelings of reward, increase mental and physical health, and decrease mortality in the giver. The investigation of the nature of these benefits, however, is still nascent, with an emphasis on outcomes rather than mechanisms. Here, we review neural and behavioral evidence suggesting that this unique profile of benefits arises from prosocial behavior's engagement of the mammalian caregiving system, which reinforces caregiving behavior and dampens threat responses. Specifically, we review the neural regions critical to caregiving and prosocial behavior as well as experimental evidence showing that prosocial behavior can causally improve correlates of mental and physical health. We suggest that prosocial behavior benefits physical and mental health by attenuating physiological stress responses and generating feelings of social connection, purpose, and meaning.
articles.keywords: Prosocial behavior; Psychology; Feeling; Helping behavior; Mental health; Developmental psychology; Social psychology; Cognitive psychology; Neural correlates of consciousness; Affect
articles.summary: 本研究综述了亲社会行为如何通过激活哺乳动物的关怀系统来改善施予者的心理健康和身体健康。神经和行为证据表明，这一过程涉及减轻生理应激反应并增强社会连接、目的感和意义感等情感体验。
